newsitem.title: DUBAI: EBI bank says offers UAE's first mutual fund.
newsitem.headline: EBI bank says offers UAE's first mutual fund.

text.p: Emirates Bank International has launched what it says is the United Arab Emirates first mutual fund, an EBI official said on Monday.

Emirates Equity Fund, which opened for subscription on June 1, has received "an excellent response from investors (individual and corporate) all over the UAE," said Suresh Kumar, EBI's chief manager for treasury and capital markets.
The fund's units are being sold at the par value of 100 dirhams until June 15, he said in a press statement. After that, a Net Asset Value will determine the offer price of the units, he said.

The minimum subscription is 10,000 dirhams and additional amounts should be in multiples of 5,000 dirhams. However, there is no limit to the amount that the UAE nationals and wholly- owned UAE companies can invest.

"Interest among non-UAE nationals, who are residents of the UAE, has been very high as expected," Kumar said. "Non-national applicants are allowed to invest in the fund up to 20 percent of its total size with a maximum limit of 500,000 dirhams per person," he said.
"In the event of oversubscription in investments from non-nationals, the fund will allocate units on a pro rata basis after June 15," Kumar said.
"In addition, the fund will also maintain a waiting list for customers who applied in amounts of 100,000 dirhams and more provided the funds are retained on call with EBI/MEB branches".
